selection_note: UPSTREAM UPGRADE BATCH 21, explicit operator size ten. Selected ten distinct included Index S1=A/S2=C assessments with concrete, varied prospective native S2 coordination hypotheses; excluded all 105 sources claimed in integrated batches 01-20 and current open Upstream PR source claims. Exact Index main pinned and per-row prospective hypothesis immutable at commit 95d9306537e0cdf6877942215a53ff679f561b7b before fresh target source/issue inspection. Order by reviewed_at descending. These are testable questions, not established defects or external publication rights.

candidates.finding: Worktree-per-builder isolation and dirty-state refusal leave integration/reconciliation to the caller. Prospective check: A builder branch prepared from an older base may be integrated or cleaned up after another sibling lands on main without detecting a now-conflicting shared/generated file.
candidates.screening_result: Current cmd_worktree handles create/audit/remove and refuses modified/untracked/ignored cleanup; merged branch deletion has explicit merged-head proof. Integration of sibling branches into a moving accepted base is delegated to Git review/caller, not an automatic operation of this helper. The predicted auto-integration gap is outside the supported mechanism. Source inspection only; no native benefit/test claimed.

candidates.finding: Registry-keyed same-node FileLock serializes Local edits by expanded filesystem path; Index explicitly excludes symlink aliases from the demonstrated guarantee. Prospective check: Two supported paths through a symlink alias and its real target may acquire distinct locks yet mutate one file concurrently, violating same-file exclusion.
candidates.screening_result: Compared the assessed FileLock Path.expand-only code with current main: canonicalize_path now calls resolve_real_path/read_link_all and resolves symlink targets and parent symlinks before Registry lookup. The preregistered alias weakness was independently addressed upstream after the assessed ref; no duplicate patch warranted. Code inspection, not a fresh native test.

candidates.finding: Read-only child tool modes and planToolBatches allow parallel nonmutating delegates while serializing mutating delegations. Prospective check: A composite or dynamically resolved child tool batch might be classified as safe for parallel execution despite a reachable filesystem mutation.
candidates.observed_native_change: Separate dev-alpha-2 server runner on exact source 1ac18ffb: source-native pnpm exec tsx --test apps/core/src/tools/batching.test.ts with regression only exit 1 (8/9 PASS; implicit custom build role wrongly parallel), then after minimal fix exit 0 (9/9 PASS); native core typecheck after documented shared build PASS. Session IDs, hashes, commands and caveats in pilots/histh-s2/INDEPENDENT_HOST_RECEIPT_2026-11-09.md.

candidates.finding: Agent-scoped Task dedup relies on canonical URI identity, deterministic Task names and create collision checks. Prospective check: Two equivalent supported issue/resource URL spellings may produce different task identities and start duplicate worker commitments.
candidates.screening_result: No canonical-key patch or verified duplicate task run. Only pinned Go source and current primary issue/PR search inspected.
candidates.blocker: CanonicalKey lowercases scheme/host and strips a trailing slash but retains explicit HTTP default ports. Semantically equivalent URL variants could create separate TaskNameForKey values; source alone cannot establish whether URI-equivalence beyond the documented caller-supplied key contract is required or whether normalization would merge intentionally distinct keys. Need first-party canonical identity fixture/maintainer contract before patch.

candidates.finding: Async TeamInbox serializes peer targets and source-thread followups with locks, references, cancellation and callbacks. Prospective check: Canceling a queued or in-flight peer job at the target/source-lock handoff may retain a lock/reference or deliver a stale callback to a later source turn.
candidates.screening_result: Inbox cancel sets terminal status; _process checks cancellation before target invocation, again after target work, and inside the source lock. Both target and source reference-counted locks are released in finally and _finish delivers terminal status once/prunes. No supported canceled-lock-retention or stale-feedback adoption path established from this source; no new test/patch warranted.

candidates.finding: Child execution binds isolated Git worktrees and conservatively retains dirty/unmerged/in-use state for later reconciliation. Prospective check: An exception between child completion and cleanup may remove or orphan the isolated worktree even though uncommitted child edits remain.
candidates.screening_result: Native contract and source evolution inspected, but no safe repro or independent runner receipt.
candidates.blocker: Current main migrated the worktree finish implementation to an opened/daemon-backed service with kept-dirty/kept-inspection-failed/kept-in-use results; wrapper alone does not demonstrate that an injected crash between child completion and daemon cleanup loses or retains dirty data. Need a pinned first-party daemon lifecycle/failed-child fixture; no claim of lost work or patch.

candidates.finding: Hashline anchors reject stale edits after a parallel writer changes the same shared coding workspace. Prospective check: A stale anchored replacement with one still-matching neighboring line could be accepted after a competing writer modifies the targeted range.
candidates.screening_result: Source-only potential TOCTOU, not observed product loss or an admitted patch.
candidates.blocker: Current hashline resolve_range reloads and syncs anchors before resolving the requested range, but a separate commit path later writes after reading the current bytes. A post-sync concurrent writer is theoretically possible; no deterministic first-party interleaving fixture or separately executed Rust runner receipt establishes stale overwrite or safe counterfactual. Do not infer a defect merely from a read/write gap.

candidates.finding: Atomic issue and workspace slot leases use process identity checks to reject duplicate task claims and permit release/reuse. Prospective check: A stale-process or PID-reuse condition may cause lease takeover while the original owner is still live, admitting duplicate work into one slot.
candidates.screening_result: Current Lease records PID plus process start identity, checks liveness, and treats confirmed PID reuse as stale; the exact reused-PID case was already merged upstream in PR #248 (2026-10-13). The frozen prediction is not a new need. No native patch/test claimed.

candidates.finding: A shared in-process WorkspaceLock prevents runner and goal entry from colliding in the same project's Git checkout. Prospective check: Two separately launched supported CLI instances for the same project may each create a fresh in-memory lock and mutate one checkout simultaneously.
candidates.screening_result: The first-party WorkspaceLock explicitly advertises in-process exclusivity, wired between runner and GoalService in one project runtime; separate independently launched CLIs are not covered by the observed S2 contract. No supported cross-process guarantee or owner demand was established; imposing a global filesystem lock would widen scope. No patch/test claimed.

candidates.finding: Per-wave promise chains serialize approval and question resolutions from independent child S1s. Prospective check: If one approval/question callback rejects, its rejected tail may prevent a subsequent legitimate child prompt from being presented.
candidates.screening_result: Current gatedApprove/gatedAsk assign the next tail to run.catch(() => undefined), healing rejected prompts before subsequent queue admission while the failed original promise still propagates to its child. The precise predicted poisoned-tail failure is already excluded. No patch/test claimed.
